title: Interior Design Salary: Award Rates, Tax, and Super for 2026–27
description: Understand interior design salary with Fair Work award rates, casual loading, tax brackets, and super. Use our calculator to convert hourly to annual pay.
salarySummary: For a full-time interior designer on 38 hours per week, the annual salary is the hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours, with super paid on top.

faqs.a: Interior designers may be covered by the Retail Award if they work for a retail employer, or by the Miscellaneous Award if they are unqualified or trade qualified and not covered by another award. Degree-qualified interior designers are often award-free and entitled to the National Minimum Wage. See the Fair Work Ombudsman’s guide on award coverage for interior designers, decorators and stylists for details.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to interior design pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $23.09 per hour (Miscellaneous Award Level 3), the casual rate is $28.86. Use the timesheet tool and check the casual loading box to see the effect.

faqs.q: What tax do interior designers pay on their salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. The calculator on this site applies these rates to your annual gross pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the interior design salary landscape

Interior design salary in Australia is shaped by the award or agreement that covers the role, the employee’s qualifications and the employer’s industry. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides a detailed guide on award coverage for interior designers, decorators and stylists. However, those rates are based on 2020 rates and are updated annually each July by the Fair Work Commission. The pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman show the current rates after the 4.75% increase from 1 July 2026 [

## How to calculate your annual interior design salary

The formula for annual gross pay is hourly rate multiplied by hours per week times 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, that is 38 hours × 52 = 1,976 hours. If you are paid an award rate, use the appropriate classification. For example, a Level 3 interior stylist with a Certificate IV under the Miscellaneous Award earns $23.09 per hour. Their annual salary is $23.09 × 1,976 = $45,626 per year. A casual employee adds 25% loading of 25% on top of the base rate, so $23.09 + 25% = $28.86 per hour, annual $57,026. The fortnightly pay is weekly pay × 2. For the full-time employee, weekly pay is $23.09 × 38 = $877.42, fortnightly $1,754.84.

## Tax and super on your interior design salary

Tax is calculated on the annual gross amount using the 2026–27 resident tax brackets: nil to $18,200; 15% to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above that. Medicare levy is 2% on taxable income. For an interior designer earning $45,000, tax is $4,000 plus 2% Medicare. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings paid on top, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The calculator on this site applies these deductions to your hourly rate and shows the take-home pay after tax and Medicare.

## Using the timesheet tool

The timesheet tool on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. Never enter a rate that already includes loading. It then shows hourly × hours per week × 52 to get annual, plus fortnightly, and then shows tax and super. Use the timesheet to see your interior design salary estimate.

## Key points to remember

- Always use the correct award rate or the National Minimum Wage if award-free. The Fair Work Ombudsman says award-free employees are entitled to the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour.

## Final note on the calculation

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 26.44 per hour, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

See [the timesheet](/) and the [reference tables](/data) for the 38-hour working.
